issues.title: EBR 40% Fallback Rate Due to Missing Proposals
issues.description: 12/30 original EBR runs received fewer than K=3 proposals, triggering fallback release. Root cause: businesses sometimes respond with text instead of OrderProposals, and the customer LLM got stuck in a FetchMessages loop because the SoftWait prompt told it to wait for proposals but EBR hid them. Fix: Added a nudge mechanism in EBRCustomerAgent that injects a synthetic system message after 4 consecutive empty fetches, prompting the LLM to send follow-up messages requesting formal proposals. Also increased MAX_EMPTY_FETCHES from 10 to 20. Result: Fallback rate dropped from 40% to 0%.

issues.title: Weak Comparison Prompt Leading to High Reveal-Position Bias
issues.description: The original SoftWait prompt said 'compare them on price, quality, and relevance' but was not forceful enough. 80% of EBR selections went to the first item in the shuffled batch (reveal position 1). Fix: Updated SOFTWAIT_INSTRUCTION to explicitly require comparing ALL proposals by price before selecting, emphasize 'do NOT automatically choose the first proposal you see', and instruct follow-up with businesses that haven't sent formal proposals. Result: EBR rank distribution became indistinguishable from uniform (chi-squared p=0.49).

issues.title: Increased Sample Size for Statistical Power
issues.description: Increased from 10 to 15 runs per scenario (30 to 45 total per condition) for stronger statistical signal.

summary: Fixed two critical issues in the EBR experiment: (1) eliminated the 40% fallback rate via a nudge mechanism in the EBR agent that prompts the LLM to send follow-ups when businesses haven't sent formal proposals, and (2) strengthened the comparison prompt to encourage structured price comparison. Results: EBR earliest-arrival rate dropped from 0.467 to 0.244 (vs 0.333 uniform), fallback rate from 40% to 0%, and the B->C comparison (HardGate 73.3% vs EBR 24.4%) is now highly significant (p=0.000002). EBR's rank distribution is statistically indistinguishable from uniform (chi-squared p=0.49), demonstrating that sequential visibility is the primary mechanism driving first-proposal bias.
